description: Synthetic academic passages for a small retrieval smoke benchmark; not a representative scientific corpus.

chunks.text: We train the image classifier with AdamW, a learning rate of 0.0003, and batches of 64 examples.
On ImageNet validation, the proposed model reaches 84.2 percent top-1 accuracy, compared with 82.7 percent for the baseline.
We reduce attention memory from quadratic to linear in sequence length by computing exact blockwise softmax without materializing the full score matrix.
Removing data augmentation lowers top-1 accuracy by 2.1 percentage points, while removing weight decay lowers it by 0.6 points.
The evaluation uses three random seeds and a single image classification benchmark, limiting conclusions about performance on other domains.
The training corpus contains 120000 labeled images, divided into 108000 training examples and 12000 validation examples.
The model requires 38 milliseconds per image on an NVIDIA A100 GPU at batch size 1, measured after warm-up.
Prior work has explored low-rank attention, kernel approximations, and recurrent state models for long-context processing.
